subject: Behavioral Economics
title: Take-the-Best Heuristic
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Take-the-Best Heuristic.

hook.text: A doctor diagnoses chest pain using just three yes-or-no questions. Her accuracy rivals complex models.

buildup.text: Gigerenzer's take-the-best rule: check the most important cue first. If it discriminates, decide. Stop.

discovery.text: More information doesn't always mean better decisions. One good cue can outperform a complex formula.

twist.text: In noisy environments with missing data, simple heuristics outperform regression models consistently.

climax.text: Simplicity isn't laziness. In complex environments, simple rules are robust where complex models overfit.

punchline.text: One good question beats ten mediocre ones.

quiz.question: When does the take-the-best heuristic outperform complex models?
options: In noisy environments with incomplete data
